name: impact_analysis
description: For a given requirement ID, lists everything that could break if the requirement is modified. Walks one-to-two hops along the downstream trace edges (SATISFIES, DERIVES_FROM, REFINES, VERIFIES) and also returns LLM-discovered semantic dependencies (SEMANTICALLY_DEPENDS_ON, CONSTRAINS) plus any hard conflicts. Each row shows the dependent requirement, the exact chain of relationship types used to reach it, whether the hop was explicit or LLM-inferred, and the tests/standards at risk, so a change-control board can estimate blast radius without hand-tracing the graph.
when_to_use: Fire this template when the user asks about the consequences of changing or removing one specific requirement. Typical phrasings: 'what breaks if I change FCC-042', 'impact of modifying REQ-PWR-017', 'who depends on STR7-NAV-014', 'change risk for requirement X', 'if we raise the undervoltage threshold on Stratos-7, what is affected'. The user must provide a single requirement id. Do not use this template for open-ended 'related to' questions — route those to Similarity Search instead.

parameters.name: req_id
parameters.description: The Requirement.id of the anchor whose blast radius we want to compute. Example values: 'FCC-042', 'REQ-PWR-017', 'STR7-NAV-014'. Extract verbatim from the user's question and preserve case.

cypher:
MATCH (anchor:Requirement {id: $req_id})
OPTIONAL MATCH path = (anchor)<-[rels:SATISFIES|DERIVES_FROM|REFINES|VERIFIES|SEMANTICALLY_DEPENDS_ON|CONSTRAINS|POTENTIALLY_CONFLICTS|CONFLICTS_WITH*1..2]-(dependent:Requirement)
WITH anchor, dependent, path,
     [r IN relationships(path) | type(r)] AS chain,
     [r IN relationships(path) | coalesce(r.discovery_method, 'explicit')] AS provenance,
     length(path) AS hop_count
OPTIONAL MATCH (dependent)-[:VERIFIED_BY]->(t:TestProcedure)
OPTIONAL MATCH (dependent)-[:REFERENCES_STANDARD]->(s:Standard)
RETURN DISTINCT
       anchor.id          AS anchor_id,
       anchor.heading     AS anchor_heading,
       dependent.id       AS dependent_id,
       dependent.heading  AS dependent_heading,
       dependent.module   AS dependent_module,
       dependent.summary  AS dependent_summary,
       chain,
       provenance,
       hop_count,
       collect(DISTINCT t.id)   AS tests_to_rerun,
       collect(DISTINCT s.name) AS standards_at_risk
ORDER BY hop_count ASC, dependent_module, dependent_id
notes: Bounded to two hops so Aura Free plans execute in well under a second on a 1000-requirement corpus. Explicit trace edges (SATISFIES, DERIVES_FROM, REFINES, VERIFIES, CONFLICTS_WITH) and LLM-discovered edges (SEMANTICALLY_DEPENDS_ON, CONSTRAINS, POTENTIALLY_CONFLICTS) are both traversed; the provenance array lets the agent tell the user which hops are human-authored versus model-inferred. Returns an empty result set (not an error) when the anchor id does not exist — the agent should then fall back to a similarity search on the wording the user used.
